rationale:
Evidence: iteration 5 (base_speed 1.2, line_loss search_left) is the best raced design so far at 81.82, up from 56.11. Oval progress rose from 0.137 to 0.318 and oval line-loss events fell to 0.15. Oval max_error is still 0.0626 on average, over the 0.06 m off-track limit, and the score spread (54 to 141) shows some oval seeds leave the track and others run far. On s-bend and slalom, line_loss_events stayed at 1 with search_left, and progress barely moved (0.1615 and 0.110). So the search direction is not the limiting factor on those tracks, and search_left is kept. Steering oscillation on the oval is 0.183, above the 0.15 guide.

Change: base_speed 1.2 to 1.0, with everything else unchanged (geometry, kp 4.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.30, sensor weights, search_left). The speed drop from 1.4 to 1.2 gave the largest gain on the oval, and the oval max_error is the one thing blocking that gain from scoring. Slower entry into the corners should reduce the peak lateral error. I am changing one group only so the effect stays attributable.

Expected result: oval max_error falls below 0.06 on more seeds, with line-loss events at 0 or near it, and oval progress at or above 0.318. Hypotheses: (a) speed 1.0 keeps oval max_error under 0.06; (b) s-bend and slalom progress stay near 0.16 and 0.11, since speed is not their limit; (c) if oval progress falls below 0.318, speed is too low and the best value is between 1.0 and 1.2. Next, if oscillation on the oval stays above 0.15 and max_error is still at or above 0.06, reduce kd to about 0.20 before changing kp. If s-bend and slalom still show one line loss, the next test is a different sensor layout (for example a wider spread or a fifth sensor forward) rather than the recovery direction.
